plan: With my private value at $49, which is the maximum possible value, my optimal strategy is to bid very close to my true value. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment, I want to bid high enough to win but not so high that I reduce my potential profit. A bid of $48.9 would ensure I win while minimizing my payment, capturing almost the full value of the prize if I win.

My private value is $44, which means I'll make money if I win and pay less than $44. In a single-round game with no history, the optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly under my true value. This prevents overpaying while still having a good chance of winning. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, other bidders might have values anywhere in that range. I'll bid $43.9 to maximize my potential profit margin.

My private value is $22. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. Since the prize is worth $22 to me, and I want to maximize potential profit, I'll bid close to but slightly below my true value. This protects against overpaying while still having a good chance of winning. I'll bid $21.9 to ensure I win in most scenarios unless another bidder values the item significantly higher.
